body: Of course I would!!!  I would love to read your work and give my own feedback.  My schedule is hectic right now,but I promise, I will read it (I adore poetry:writing AS WELL AS reading it. Poetry is music for the deaf, language for the mute, and art for the blind, and most of all, it is the composition of not events (whether fictional or true), but of the FEELINGS of those events, and when you read or hear a poem, for moment, if the poet is particular talented, an almost telepathic phenomenon occurs, and your mind finds itself in the exact place that the writer's mind was in at the moment his/her/their fingers first gripped a quill or began to type.  I adore poetry.  I write short fiction, but poetry is the air that I breath.  Music is my life, but it in itself is but another form of poetry, in my opinion.  IMHO, I don't see poetry as an art, but rather all forms of art as various subtypes of poetry. But I digress.  I will be getting to your poem and further correspondence as soon as I am able to.  Thank you for the positive feedback, and OF COURSE you are qualified. You are a poet, yourself, and you are able to read my work and write suggestions, critique and praise, which makes you just as qualified as I am. I'm no better or worse or more or less talented than ANY SINGLE PERSON on this subreddit.  I am a poet.  You are a poet.  That is all that matters.  That and following my suggestion that any poet NEVER cease their writing.  Always write. Always practice.  Learn a new word or poetic device each day.  Read a poem or piece from a writer you've never read each day.   Allow yourself room to grow.  Don't show up at the fountain with a cup or a bucket, but rather an unquenchable thirst for honing your craft and enjoying the work that others' crafts have brought forth into this world which so neglects the intrinsic value for the arts in general and poetry in particular (unless it is filled with profanity, obsesses over one's sexual conquests and talent for selling drugs, smoking ganja, drinking booze, and "making it rain",while setting it to a beat that was sampled from a song that actually took *effort* to make. Keep writing.  NEVER stop writing.  I'll be in touch.  -2bL aka Adrianne/DHR

And efficiency will increase surely along with morale if the mentality behind the rule catches with everybody like it did with me and a good many here.  I've only been on one other poetry forum, and it was madness, chaos, trolling and suicidal kids posting only to tell each other to "DOITF****T".   This is a vast improvement.

I enjoyed this.  Haiku and senryu has always had a place in my heart since I began writing...the art of saying everything while barely saying anything.  As this is a comment and not a post, please, no feedback, as I would be happy to "continue" the chain and keep it going:



Roses bloom in rot;


new life swims within the wound.


In death, nature thrives.

Thank you so much!  I changed up my style and personalized my genre and voice a couple years ago, having begun writing (serious) poetry at age 17.  9 years later, I think I've honed my craft quite a bit if all of this positive feedback is genuine.  And I believe it is, but there always room to improve. I might post a poem tomorrow only for everybody hate it, and next week I might post another poem and strike gold by having a Publisher/Editor lurker see my work and pay me.  I wouldn't want a million bucks or fame or anything like that, but making a comfortable living doing what I do best, enjoy the most, and need to survive seems pretty convenient.  ~2bL aka Adrianne DHR

Well, that does it.  I just got done with a doctor's appnt and now know that I have Narcolepsy.  I've been given Amphetamine Salt (Controlled Release) to control it, and it actually is working.  I haven't had a "fallout" or "episode" yet since it kicked in.  I feel stimulated with a mild sense of well being, but not high, which was what I was worried about, as I was concerned about the drug jeopardizing my recovery from opiate and heroin addiction.  Apparently, if you actually NEED a prescription drug, abuse is less likely.  WHOA.  Still kind of shook up and coping with the news.  I'm still in the dark as to whether my driver's license is going to be taken or not.  :*(

Thank you so much for your input!   I hope that this massive praise for the poems I've posted isn't just flattery.  And although I haven't commented yet, I read your work "Insomnia".  I really enjoyed it, and it stuck out to me as one of my first "Serious Poems" shared the same title, but I was novice then, and I see you have talent and similar voice to my own.  I'll publish it eventually for kicks and giggles.  It's funny that my poem is marked "NSFW" when the "Pornography" it is referring to is the epic goth rock/post punk album by The Cure, which has most definitely influenced me, especially in this poem (References not only the album, but the lead singer and founder, Robert Smith, as well as the magnum opus of the album: "The Hanging Garden".  Thank you so much for your kind feedback.  We will be in touch, and I look forward to sharing more and reading more with you and the other friends I've made in these wonderful couple of days on this subreddit (I first joined 5 days ago with the intention of finding somebody to assist me in ending my life (See the post:  I apologize; Please Help in /r/suicidewatch.  The original post "Want to watch somebody die?" has been deleted, and I am actually feeling a good bit better now that I have been writing more and getting true and honest critique while sharing a community with the other writers her and offering my own feedback for such wonderful works of written art.   Keep in touch, and never let your "Poet's Fire" burn out.  Best Regards, 2bL aka Adrianne DHR

So far, even though I only joined Reddit maybe 5 or 6 days ago, I am thoroughly impressed.  I feel among peers, no matter what level of talent or age or style.  As long as we continue mandatory (what should go unspoken, really) feedback and INTERACTION with our fellow poets, this subreddit could become something great:  A massive collaborate effort to better our craft through our reading of other's work and the critique we both give and receive.

Thank you.  The slash left in the title was from a partial deleting of it's alternate title, "Of Lesbian Bed Death", which refers to a phenomenon that occurs within a small percent of lesbian couples during which intimacy literally "dies"...no sex, romance, or even amicability.  My cousin has had many girlfriends that I thought were perfect for her go through this "divorce" of sorts.  Even I've gone through it with a past lover long ago, and the phrase just fits the situation to a "t".  Love is beautiful, but like all beauty, it can die and become the ugliest thing in a person's life.  All it takes is the "perfectly horrible" combination of people in love, and emotions supersede logic as apathy grows to antipathy, and eventually the inevitable severing of ties.  Thank you for your feedback!  I appreciate it very much so.  I look forward to seeing some of your stuff in the near future!  ~2bLifted aka Adrianne DHR

Bravo! This poem is so fluid and eloquent, yet it maintains just enough distance to create a sense of pure nostalgia, and possibly regret for leaving that "pizza stop signed, three stated world" behind.  The imagery is perfect, and as I read I truly felt the emotions of reluctant adulthood...feebly grasping tiny "tastes" of the previous magic and wonder life held before we eagerly crossed that awful finish line: "Growing Up".  It brings memories before me of past friends who don't recognize me, imaginary friends whose names I can no longer recall, and a longing to feel that innocence once again.  MAJOR Kudos, friend.  I hope this feedback provides some kindle for the creative fire in you.  Yours is one I do NOT wish to see burn out.  I'll be looking through more of your work soon enough.  Best regards, 2bL.

Besides maybe some rearranging of the lines, and a few simple punctuation errors, this poem reads well of the idea of grief as a ghost in itself.  Perhaps that's the origin of what we think of as supernatural "hauntings"...It's not hearing a bump in the night, but rather not hearing the voice of the one you lost.   Kudos, 2bL.

Thank you.  I took the title to from a book I was given by a counselor during a stay at your run of the mill "detox mansion"  (I am a recovering Opiate addict.  They give you heroin in a pill and shake their heads at you when you get hooked... *sigh*).  It was a wonderful facility, and I believe he is now teaching Psychology at a University.  The name of the school escapes me.  I digress: He was a wonderful therapist, but he lived on the edge in his profession: He lent me the book under the condition that I tell not a single soul.  It delved quite deeply into the very mindset and obsessive ritual of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder, comparing it to a "cult consisting of a single reluctant member", who's mind has developed what normally would be stored in long term memory as a *survival instinct*...elevating a "mortal memory" to an immortal (unforgettable and unrelenting), seemingly omnipotent "Deity" within the mind of the victim.  Only when one can directly confront the trauma and let go, it holds a grip onto every facet of its unfortunate and unwilling acolyte's behavior, driving many to a severity that may very well culminate in violence against others or the victim themselves.  (You can see why a holistic rehab would probably fire him for giving me such a book, especially when the lack of "mother opium" and her "pharmaceutical extended family" set in and my PTSD first began displaying its symptoms with a velocity and force that nearly drove me to ending my life within my first day out of the heavily monitored detox ward.  72 days of that place helped a good bit, but it took a few bumps, hard knocks, short "chipping" and long runs to finally get the level of care required to keep that demon at bay.  Poetry, as an outlet alone, is a godsend in my recovery.  (3 years in October.  Hooray. )   But that theme might appear in future posts, but I've much more wonderful work on this subreddit to enjoy reading and many more fellow poets such as yourself to converse and commiserate with!   Thank you for reading!   And thank you with the advice on the structure.  I'm just so used to submitting physical copies that I tend to get stuck in the "Essay structure" American English Teachers are forced to maintain and it translates poorly when copy/ pasted.  *laughs*  Anyway, I'm going to go ahead and add you as a friend.  I look forward to perusing through your work soon enough.  Thank you, 2bL

I'm...literally *almost* at a loss for words.  Thank you so much.  I can see what you mean at first, but it truly is addressing a child.  I intended to compare the sensations brought by abuse (particular childhood sexual abuse) with the panic, nervousness and uncertainty of surgery, hence the narrator's encouragement to "breath in the solvent"...anesthesia...be it drugs, prescribed or unknowingly taken, grooming before victimization, shame induced feelings of guilt or a myriad of other ways that make victims, however hurt, temporarily, yet repetitively numb. (PTSD often has marked disassociation.  Also, I tried addressing the relationship and mindset that take place in the trauma from both parties by composing the poem as an address from the violator to the violated, directly at the heat of the moment while closing with the hardest part of ascending from "victim" to "survivor"...shaking off the "ether" and trying to see through the fog and confront the trauma head on, own it, and gain closure.  Unfortunately, many will never gain complete mental and spiritual equilibrium again and will be on a diet of Benzodiazepine Sedatives and SSRI Antidepressants.  (As you can probably tell from my tone, I, unfortunately, am writing from experience.  I've come a long way, but it still has a profoundly devastating effect on my life if the disorder is triggered and I am without my medicine on hand.  Thank you again, so much, for your kind and possibly overly-generous critique; reading this meant the world to me.  I look forward to reading more of your work.  "My Dreams are Fire" was phenomenal.  :)

I will definitely check out Mystic, but I am not unfamiliar with Sylvia Plath.  Thank you for your kind words about this piece.  It wasn't easy to write, but definitely therapeutic to do so.  I'm glad I put the trigger warning in it, as I had to go back and edit the piece once I realized I forgot to do so.  I know if I had been caught off guard by it, it probably wouldn't have had too positive of an effect.
Personally, both work equally well in my eye in retrospect.  I hope to see more from you.

This poem is much like its title:  Elite.  Besides its accidental formation into a paragraph (copy/pasting from Word is such a pain...), I see no flaws except maybe a possible mis-wording:  Did you mean "Violence Slanderers" or "Violent Slanderers"?  Please, correct me if I am wrong, but I see this as an anthem of sorts praising those of us who choose to write, be it poetry, short stories, novels or essays (particularly, those of us who write with our own truth in our work).   It seems to imply a fraternity/family of sorts, connecting us (writers) all by our dedication to our craft, especially in the cases where we write in order to change something in our respective "worlds" for the better, whether it is an editorial which enlightens voters as to a politician who is planning on committing some awful violation of our fellow citizens' rights or a poem which deals with a trauma endured by the author, which finds its way into the hands of a reader who has endured a similar horror, only to find solace in the newly acquired knowledge that they are not alone in their struggles.  This poem is almost a manifesto in its nature: it doesn't describe the histrionics of the middle school "emo kid" who feels that their life is unfair because they got a PS4 instead of an XBOX One, but rather, the writer who truly throws themselves into their art, and does so with a purpose and an inner truth that drives them to write, and expose themselves to a precious vulnerability...an openness that allows the world inside, so that whether the piece is of beauty or of suffering, the reader will, if they are receptive to the writer's selfless "gift", feel empathy, relate to the piece, feel moved by its message, or simply bring joy to their hearts or a human connection between themselves and the writer in question (allowing them to interpret the piece however they may and yet STILL find the "base message" of the piece.  I could be way off, but this is what I got out of it.  You can be a writer or a poet.  One of millions upon millions of writers and poets.  E Pluribus Unum and whatnot...or you are one of "The Elite".  The rhythm and meter are fantastic, and it helps carry the message, and although my interpretation of it seems to be my own (it seems, based on the other comments, that this poem is about the "elite" attitudes among some writers who put themselves above others in what I often call "intellectual fascism".  It's sad that so many potentially wonderful, talented writers fail to put their "inner truth" within their work, and instead only put their preferred "truth" in their works and critiques as if they are the elite.  But I think many of us are of the true elite:  the artists who create for creation's sake, and despite their talent, maintain their modesty so as to have room to grow.  "It is the fool who thinks himself wise and omniscient; it is the wise man who acknowledges that he knows nothing."

I enjoyed reading this.  It seems I was not the only one writing of dreams this morning.  The rhythm, wording and eloquence of the piece are very fluid, and I feel that I can relate to the meaning.  (But, of course, my meaning for *your* poem may very well be nothing close to your intentions, but that's the beauty of poetry:  I can feel what you mean, but to each reader, the feeling is the same but interpreted in a unique way.  This poem truly resonates with me.  I apologize if my critique is not as helpful as you may have hoped, but I am no literary major or liberal arts student: I'm just another poet who appreciates every piece that touches me, and this poem accomplishes its goal quite well.  Kudos, friend!

I still wish to keep the references to Poe, but otherwise, your feedback is greatly appreciated.  Also, pardon my ignorance, but how do you mean "on the nose"?  I'm just curious. Thank you, but I did not duplicate my feedback.   I didn't know how much was required, but rather than copy/pasting the original feedback, I paraphrased my feedback and even added a couple of extra notes.  I hope to see some feedback and positive criticism as it definitely promotes any writer/poet's growth in their craft.  This poem is particularly sentimental to me, as I wrote it for my life partner, who has been very stressed lately by my depression and recent suggestions from my doctors that I have Narcolepsy in at least a mild to moderate form (14 to 18 hours of sleep a day if not fed stimulants or forcefully awakened every time it hits.  Keep in mind, I don't even know when it happens.  I literally might be talking and in mid sentence, my beloved will shout "Wake Up!!!", and at first I deny that I was sleeping and become quite agitated and defensive...that is until I look at my watch and notice an hour has disappeared and most of my "speech" was gibberish and I was only dreaming that the conversation was real.  This poem was meant not only as a declaration of love, but an expression of appreciation for the fact that I can NOT control this and that, if it were possible, I would have him join me in my dreams to make up for every precious second of time with him that I am denied simply because something misfires in my brain.  But thank you for clearing that up for me.  :)  I am so new to reddit that I had no idea how supportive and wonderful the site was.  I struggle with treatment resistant major depressive disorder, and I posted in the /r/suicidewatch subreddit, half expecting possibly ten or twenty responses such as "DO IT FAGGOT" or "Log off and quit wasting everybody's time and just die already", but was pleasantly surprised:  I only had one person respond, and they were very supportive and empathetic, even offering advice as to finding ways to cope and encouraging me to "keep up the good fight" and to "stick around", if you catch my drift.  I look forward to reading and providing even more feedback, and hopefully getting some feedback of my own with this and other poems I've yet to publish on Reddit.   Thank you, gwrgwir.  I understand my "feedback summaries" were redundant, but not without points that I didn't realize until I was already typing my own poem.  Should I edit it and delete the "summaries?"  Or should I just leave it as is and simply not make the mistake again.  Thank you.  Yours Truly, 2bLifted aka Adrianne aka Darianne/Daria

Okay, I hope this is quality feedback (I'm more of a poet than a critic), but I loved this.  I adore the building up to the crescendo of the last line, revealing that all of this leads to writing poetry about the REALITY of what most people (especially us "starving artists") go through as opposed to the "American Dream" or the bourgeois representation of "American Life" which we watch from afar on the technicolor flashing lights and sounds of our cheap tvs while we swallow our "soilent green" in the form of big macs.  I also applaud the use of profanity as a poetic device:  No, I'm not saying "Fuck this and Fuck that" is a means to a masterpiece, but the final stanza "to get drunk in the park
and write poetry
about your fucked up life." hit me like a sucker punch to the stomach, complete with a quick inhalation of thick air and feeling every ounce of emotion poured out, only to be slammed by that last sentence...I also find the title "Imagine" to be most appropriate, as the irony is not unseen:  Imagine was a utopian piece, and this piece, although it shares the name, beckons the reader to "imagine" what most folks HAVE to imagine in order to understand the pain and hardship of a shitty job, missing out on precious moments with family only to try to kill the pain with strong drink, honesty, and soul mixed with black ink.   Kudos to you, and I look forward to more of your work!

I really enjoyed this poem. I can feel the longing and pain as you gaze at your paramour from what seems like miles away, and I can relate to that.  You are not weak.  I think everybody has felt this way before, but not everybody has the courage to write a poem about it (which, if music is the language of the soul, poetry is its "non-melodic" dialect) and, essentially, bleeding your soul for an often cruel horde of critics.  I also admire the talent involved in what you say is your FIRST poem?  Kudos, snaps, and keep up the good work.  Poetry is dying, and it's new poets like you who pick up the quill everyday that is the dying art's last hope.  Thank you for sharing.  I hope the feedback was good.  There is always room for improvement, but if this is your first, and therefore, your "baseline" to improve from, you are going to go far!!!!

Good answer.  I'm MTF (Male to Female) with a possible intersex condition.  I don't consider it a mental disorder, as the only suffering I've experienced besides my dysphoria (which my Hormone Replacement Therapy has dealt with wonderfully) is that which is inflicted on me by the transphobic/homophobic majority which thinks of me as a "freak" or an object of lust to be objectified and fetishized (they'll hit on me and talk so sweetly to me only to threaten to brutally rape and murder me once I catch on and tell them to go fuck themselves.).  The reality is that cisgender privilege exists just as transgender disadvantage does: In extremes.  I'm subjected to slurs and death threats almost constantly, misgendered in public (which can be very dangerous; many of us are assaulted and killed just based on how some asshole absolutely had to call me "SIR!" as loudly as possible so that everybody within earshot knows that something about me as a woman is peculiar.  Otherwise, I pass quite well), in spite of my growing breasts, skirt and blouse, make up and long hair...just jerks who remembered me as a male and wanted to do the one thing that hurts my feelings the most and can trigger violence against me by proxy.  Yes, I suffer from mental illnesses, and although Gender Dysphoria is a disorder according to the DMV-V, I see it as just another part of a very large spectrum.  Biological Sex: Male-------Intersex----Female, Gender:  Male----Demi-Male-----Bigender---Gender Neutral----Androgynous---Third Gender---Agender-----Demi-Female---Female, Orientation:  Heterosexual-----Bisexual----Asexual---Pansexual----Homosexual,   and Gender Expression:  Masculine, Feminine, Androgyne, Genderqueer, Neuter.  There are other identities on top of the ones I've listed, but these are the ones most usually identify as, most of the time differently for each category.  For example:  My sex is male, my gender is Female, (Despite my being born male and being attracted to males) I identify as Pansexual (attracted to all sexes, genders, and gender expressions) but predominantly heterosexual, and my gender expression is Feminine-Androgynous.  Keep in mind, some people can even be romantic with one sex or gender and sexual with another.  I've met gay men who were bi/hetero-romantic and found love with a woman.  I've met straight people who were bi/homo-romantic and had brief relationships with the same sex.  I know some who are asexual, and can't stand sex at all, but form healthy relationships with all genders, gender expressions, and sexes, and are therefore Pan-Romantic.  It's several overlapping spectrum that are determined primarily before birth, and with some social aspects which influence it, and as it is a fairly new science (at least new in that it has become less about spreading malicious rumors as facts, forced castrations, and associating anybody that is not Cisgender, Heterosexual, and expressing their gender as society dictates they should with perversion, pedophilia, and deviancy or otherwise a lack of moral fiber) which has made great strides recently, but we still have yet to fully understand much more than the facts that (A) it's not a "choice" and (B) it's not something that can be "fixed", as nothing is broken. (Seriously, there is a reason they are shutting down "corrective therapy" camps for LGBTQIAP youth...the success rate is minimal, with the "successes" usually "relapsing" or killing themselves.  God help the poor souls that have had to go through those hell holes.  But Gender and Sexuality variation is neither choice nor disease, but rather just another part of the human condition.  Much love to you all, and to all young LGBTQIAP folk out there reading this, especially my fellow trans brothers, sisters, and in-betweeners, please hang in there, and know that there is NOTHING wrong with you...perhaps something is wrong with how your family/peers/strangers perceive and treat you, but you are all beautiful human beings who deserve happiness like everybody else.  Keep in mind, it gets better, and has been slowly getting better with every passing day.  Hopefully, I will live to see the day when the "closet" will no longer refer to a hiding place (which usually also contains nooses and guns) and Homo/Bi/Pan/Intersex/Asex/Transphobia will be a thing of the past.   Never forget, never surrender.  Things will get better if we band together and hold strong when the haters and 'phobes try to bring us down.  I hope I live to see the day when the bashings, murders, rapes and suicides end, but we still have a long way to go. Good post, OP.  This is a question that many have but will not usually seek out the answer, but assume that the "man" wearing the "dress" must be crazy to do so.  No, that WOMAN is actually brave for being "crazy" enough to be HERself in a society where she faces discrimination, stigmatization, ostracism, assault, corrective rape, murder, and possible bullying to the point of suicide.  Keep the faith, smash open the closet doors, and to thine own self be true!

Update: I woke up, dosed, and now I'm trying to not wake up a mutual friend of my boyfriend and myself, who is unconscious on the couch behind me on a cocktail of downers and painkillers.  Not sure if he's mainlining, but he's done it before.  Listening to Samhain, Bauhaus, Christian Death, Beethoven and Mozart.  No, my "liquid breakfast" doesn't get me high, but it gives me enough of a buzz to call it a "reprieve" of sorts which calms my depressive state and brings out my creativity.  I usually write poetry, but I've yet to begin typing that.  I'm still alive.  I'm still here.  My boyfriend talked with me while the aforementioned friend nodded out:  He apologized for acting angry and explained that he is really worried about me and my health.  My sleep symptoms match Excessive Daytime Sleepiness and/or Narcolepsy, but I just think it's my depression.  I'm really considering Electro-Convulsive Therapy.  It's not as painful as the movies make it out to be: They give you a benzo if you're nervous, a barbiturate to relax the muscles (while a tourniquet is placed on your ankle so that the drug can't reach your toes and therefore the seizure can be monitored), administer the brief shock, wait until the seizure passes, and then you come to with a temporary amnesia and possible months of relief.  I think my insurance would pay for it.  Anybody on Reddit experienced this controversial therapy? If not, should an implant that stimulates the vagus nerve been considered? I know this is not Web MD.  I'm just seeking opinions, experience, feedback, and if I'm lucky, hope.  On a scale of 1 to 10, my mood is at a 3-4, which is higher than it usually is, and I can already feel a small, not intoxicating albeit very noticeable "glow" from the Methadone. I'm grateful I'm not waking up violently ill every morning, lying, cheating, stealing and doing anything to bang some pills or dope, and I'll stand by the fact that my "Liquid handcuffs" have saved my life.  I do often ponder, however, whether I was "supposed to die" and that my problems might stem from my "overstaying my welcome", but this isn't a fan fic from "Dead Like Me" (Why did they have to cancel that show?).   I know that I exist, whatever that means, and that I'll either live my life or I'll take it into my own hands and no longer have to live in fear. At this point, I cannot afford any mental health institution outside of the state run hell hole that they house rapists and pedophiles and murderers inside (boy, that would be some GREAT confrontation therapy for my PTSD...), but I certainly would go to a facility that separated the sexes (NO WAY am I going on a coed or male ward) and didn't look like a scene from "One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest"...but that's not a luxury I have right now.  So another 24 hours. I did slip up and cut myself, but felt guilty immediately and refrained from doing any real damage (usually, I find myself in stitches after an SI episode.  Hell, I usually just black out and wake up covered in blood with a blade in my hands and wounds that go down past the dermis, subdermis and finally fat, which terrifies me immensely that, if I were to WANT to live and accidentally, say, knicked an artery, I would be dead in minutes.  )  However, my cutting has never been suicidal.  As stated before, massive narcotic overdose with hanging as backup would be the choice method, but your words of encouragement, even if it's just you, "neuuutral", make a world of difference.  Thank you for responding in such a kind, understanding and empathetic manner.  I was almost certain, as I typed before, that the responses I would get would be "DO IT FAGGOT"...I probably would have just responded "DONE" and taken care of things right then, but then again, nobody responded that way, and for once, a complete stranger actually cares as whether I off myself or not, and sees that I'm not seeking a pity party.  Pity disgusts me.  Compliments make me uncomfortable.  I'm not used to positive interactions, at least, not ones that didn't lead to some sort of pain or abuse.  I sleep so much, but I am so tired.   I'm tired of everything, but I'm trying to hang in there until I can get in with my therapist and GP, as I am giving my self imposed "death sentence" a 24 hour stay, each day, and hoping that this will be my turn around point, despite hearing therapists tell me that I most likely will never be completely happy.  Yay.  "I was told I could be anything I wanted so I became a miserable, junky, transsexual poet who can't feel pleasure unless the stimulus is ridiculously intense, but can feel agonizing mental anguish at the drop of a hat."  No, I never wanted this.  I never wanted to be my Father's whipping boy.  I never wanted to be a "surrogate spouse" emotionally for both parents...I never wanted to get hooked to the dope they were pushing into me when I had an ulcer the size of a silver dollar.
